chunks: And from him, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah, who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: "Indeed, a man from the Ansar married while he was in the state of Ihram, so the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) annulled his marriage."

key_terms.الْأَنْصَارِ: The Ansar, the helpers of the Prophet from Medina
key_terms.مُحْرِمٌ: One in the state of Ihram, a ritual state for Hajj or Umrah

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on marriage contracted while in the state of Ihram?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the annulment (*faskh*) of marriage for a man who contracts it while in the state of Ihram, citing a specific precedent involving a companion from the Ansar. In Shia jurisprudence, this ruling highlights the suspension of certain legal capacities during the sacred state of pilgrimage, emphasizing that the prohibitions of Ihram extend beyond ritual acts to civil contracts. The narration serves as a foundational evidence for the principle that conditions of Ihram temporarily invalidate the validity of marriage for the male party.
